An ancient place, mentioned in the so-called Stadiasmus Maris Magni, that was probably a promontory (cape) and can likely be identified with the modern İblis Burnu (Cape İblis/Cape Angistro on the Turkish coast of the Gulf of Fethiye).
Eneolithic and early Bronze Age burial ground in the Northwest Caucasus with about 40 mounds located 3km northwest of Tsarskaya.
The site of a temple of Apollo administered by Colophonians and active from the seventh century B.C. to the fourth century A.D.
An ancient city of Arcadia in the Peloponnese. The site of ancient Kleitor lies at the western end of a valley; modern Kleitoria lies at the eastern end.
An ancient settlement, located on the Athos/Akte peninsula.
The so-called "Minoan Villa" of Klimataria is located on the 80-meter-high hill of Manares (Μάναρες) on the road from Piskokefalo (Πισκοκέφαλο) to Sitia (Σητεία).
An ancient name for a mountain, attested in primary sources. It is possibly to be identified with the Jabal Isbil in modern Yemen.
A burial ground near the modern town of Kislovodsk in the North Caucasus. The site contains 270 burials associated with the Iron Age Koban culture and the early medieval Sarmatians and Alans.

A Roman fortification located about a kilometer south of the modern German village of Kneblinghausen that was excavated at the beginning of the 20th century and is thought to date to the early period of Roman military engagement in the region.

Knowth is a Neolithic passage grave of Brú na Bóinne in the valley of the River Boyne in Ireland. The site, covering almost a hectare, is comprised of a central, large mound (Site 1) and 17 smaller satellite tombs.

An ancient temple complex of the Khmer Empire, Koh Ker is also known as Lingapura or Chok Gargyar. The site is located in the Srayong commune of Preah, Vihear province's Kulen district. The site was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage site in September 2023 and covers some 1,187 ha.
Koi Krylgan Kala is an archaeological site in Uzbekistan. At the site are the remains of a temple complex associated with the Chorasmian Dynasty, which was destroyed approximately 200 BC.
An ancient people, tribe, or cultural group. Located: R. Arda valley BUL/GRE.

An ancient river mentioned only by Pausanias, who describes it, along with the Elektra, as lying between Andania and Kyparissia in Messenia. RE declines to identify it with a specific modern river other than to assert that it must have been a tributary of the ancient Balyra. BAtlas 58 labels a river stretch corresponding to the upper course of the modern Mavrozoumena river as mapped and named in O
Kokino is a Bronze Age archaeological site located in the Republic of Macedonia. The earliest occupational evidence belongs to the early second millennium BC.
The Socotra archipelago in the Indian Ocean was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2008 on account of its biodiversity.
The Gulf of Mannar is a shallow bay that is part of the Laccadive Sea in the Indian Ocean. It is situated between the southeastern tip of India and the west coast of Sri Lanka.
An Attic asty deme belonging to the Aegeis phyle.
An Attic deme, located on Mount Pentelicon near Hecale or Michaleza.
An ancient settlement in the Troad, modern Beşiktepe in Turkey.
An ancient settlement of Mysia, located about 3 kilometers northwest of modern Beyçayırı in the Marmara region of Turkey.

Pausanias states that the Kolonos Hippios is a hill that marks the first point that Oedipus reached in Attica. It was a sacred area with rites devoted to both Poseidon and Athena, as well as a hero shrine sacred to Peirithous and Theseus, Oedipus and Adrastus. Antigonus destroyed the shrine of Poseidon.
An ancient city of Cilicia Trachea.
A promontory on the northeast coast of Sardinia, listed by Ptolemy. Its modern name is Capo Figari.
Part of the ancient city of Alexandria where the Roman theater and baths are located.
An ancient people, tribe, or cultural group. Located: Cape Comorin.
Settlement and glassmaking site in northern India, inhabited and in use during the first millennium BCE.
A settlement in Cappadocia located among "fairy chimney" rock formations.
An ancient people, tribe, or cultural group. Located: S. Caterina di Pittinuri.
An Attic asty deme of the Hippothontis phyle.
Kostyrino (Ukraine) is included as numbered feature 82 on Barrington Atlas map 87 K2.
Gsell (AAA, whence BAtlas) reported a Roman village at modern Koubba de Sidi Hamza in Algeria, covering an area of 34 hectares and including fortifications.
A prepalatial cemetery on the island of Crete that includes three tholos tombs and one rectangular tomb.
A promontory of the island of Cyprus, identified tentatively by scholars with the modern Cape Zevgari.

Mentioned in ancient sources, the Kourias promontory on Cyprus' southern coast probably corresponds to the northern, higher elevation portion of the modern Akrotiri peninsula before a thin stretch of ocean separating it from an island in antiquity filled in, creating the modern Limassol Salt Lake.
An ancient city of Egypt on the west bank of the Nile, known as Qis or Kis in Egyptian, Cusae or Kusai in Greek. The modern associated location id El Qusiya.
A small promontory on the modern Libyan coast of the Gulf of Sidra on and around which the Brega Seaport complex (Marsa Brega/Marsā al Burayqah) now stands.
Kranae is an island off the coast of Gytheio.
An ancient settlement near modern Argostoli on the island of Kefalonia.
Late Scythian burial site on the Lower Dnieper River containing burials dated to the 3rd century BCE-2nd century CE.
The Krathis is a river of Achaea. Achaean Aegae lies close to the river course, which is discussed by Herodotus, Strabo, and Pausanias.
Kretopolis, an ancient settlement of Pisidia discussed by both Diodorus Siculus and Ptolemy.
Kriou Metopon Pr. ("The Ram's Forehead) is the modern Cape Sarych, the southernmost point of Ukraine.
The modern Krishna river in India was known to Ptolemy as Maisolos.
Krokeai was a settlement in southern Laconia.
The Crocus field was a plain in Achaia Phthiotis, where Philip II of Macedon won a major victory over the Phokians and Athenians in 353/2 B.C.
Kromna was a Milesian apoikía located on the Paphlagonian coast of the Black Sea, the modern Tekkeönü.
Burial site in the Northern Caucusus containing 130 burials dated to the Middle-Late Bronze Age (2200-1650 BCE).
A fortified settlement in the chora of Chersonesos Taurike, dating from the Late Classical and Hellenistic periods, and reused in the early Medieval period.
According to the Babylonian topographical text Tintir = Babylon, Kullab was one of the six city districts of the eastern half of the inner city of Babylon and it contained four temples.
Kululu Kalesi is a proposed location of ancient Artulu.
According to the Babylonian topographical text Tintir = Babylon, Kumar was one of the four city districts of the western half of the inner city of Babylon and it contained seven temples.
The modern Kor/Kur river in Iran is possibly to be identified as the upper course of the ancient Araxes river in Koile Syria.
A large Scythian burial mound that dates to the seventh and sixth centuries B.C.
Kuruçay Höyük is a fortified settlement site of the Late Chalcolithic period (ca. 4200–3100 BCE)
An imperial dynasty roughly contemporary with the early Roman empire that controlled an area stretching from Margiana in the northwest through the Punjab in the southeast.
An ancient city of Lycia and the chief settlement in the region between Antiphellos and Myra.
Mentioned by Polybius, the Kyathos river is probably to be identified with the modern Dimikos, which is located in the modern Greek Aetolia-Acarnania Regional Unit.

The Kybele Sanctuary at Kapikaya is a rock-cut sanctuary sacred to Kybele, approximately 6 km from Pergamon, and is included in the UNESCO World Heritage site "Pergamon and its Multi-Layered Cultural Landscape".
A mountain in Arcadia (Greece), still known as Kyllene today.

An ancient fortified settlement of Achaia Phthiotis, located between the modern Greek towns of Palaia Giannitsou, Pappas, and Perivoli in the Phthiotis Regional Unit, Thessaly. The unexcavated site lies at an altitude of 700m, comprising three hills just north of a chapel of the Agia Paraskevi.
Kyparissia was an ancient settlement of Messenia.
A deme of Attica located near Pousi Kaloyerou.
Kythnos is an island in the Aegean Sea and one of the Cyclades.
Küllüoba Höyüğü is the site of a large settlement mound dating from the Chalcolithic period and continuing to the Early Bronze Age.

A Roman timber amphitheater dating from the first to fifth centuries, the Künzing Roman amphitheater measured 46 by 40 meters. The site was discovered during excavations carried out in 2003 and 2004. The archaeological site is no longer visible but a reconstructed evocation of the ancient structure marks the location.
A small site in Kurdistan, Iraq, consisting of a high and low mound with remains from the fourth and early third millennium BCE.
A place from the TAVO Index

La Alcudia refers to an area in the valley of the Río Alcudia where mineral resources were extracted in the late republican and early imperial periods. These resources included silver, lead, copper, and mercury.
Natural sources of silver were exploited in the area of La Bastide-l'Eveque in antiquity. Numerous sculptural and epigraphic finds have been made in the area.

A large necropolis excavated under rescue conditions in the 20th century. Grave goods indicated a long period of use, stretching from as early as the third century CE to as late as the sixteenth. The site is located in the French commune of Laudun-l'Ardoise, near the confluences of the Tave, Céze, and Rhône rivers.
The modern town of La Carolina in Spain's Jaén province is located near a series of ancient mines (copper, lead, and silver) and metallurgical processing sites.
The so-called "Torraccio della Cecchina" is a Roman funereal monument dating to the second century A.D. It is located at the ninth kilometer of the modern Via Nomentana.
At La Celsa (12.7 km of the Via Flaminia) are the remains of a cylindrical drum mausoleum that was likely once part of a larger funereal complex.
The principal archaeological remains found in the "La Cuma, Monte Rinaldo" site are those of a late Republican sanctuary dating to the third through first centuries B.C.
Phoenician port located at the mouth of the Segura River on Spain's Mediterranean coast.
A pre-Roman emporion of the Aude valley.
"La Loggia" refers to a squared tower that is a part of the polygonal masonry curtain wall of Norba.
An Early Bronze Age village in Sicily.
La Temple de la Madeleine, Geneva

The oldest Christian church in the city of Geneva, the Temple de la Madeleine site has been in continuous use as a church since the 5th century. The current structure on the site dates to the 15th century.
An Illyrian tribe that lived near Scodra.
Labonia is a river included on the Peutinger map. It may be identifiable with the modern Lavanestro.
Labraunda is an archaeological site located in Caria, just west of Ortaköy, Turkey. The site was sacred to both Carians and Mysians.
Labyrinthos is a name applied by Greek authors, notably Herodotus and Strabo, to describe a monumental funerary temple at Hawara.
The Capo Colonna, the ancient Promunturium Lacinium, is a cape of Calabria located near Crotone.
Laconicus Sinus is a gulf located in the southeastern Peloponnese of Greece.
Lactodorum was a fortified Roman settlement along Watling Street covering an area of ca. 11.25 ha.

An ancient lake in Latium that was the site of a Roman military victory in 496 BC; the precise location of the lake cannot be determined, although some scholars place its location at Pantano Secco near Frascati, Italy.

Ladispoli is a modern toponym; it is a comune of the Metropolitan City of Rome and is situated 35 kilometers (22 miles) west of Rome, on the Mediterranean Sea coast. In terms of the ancient landscape, present-day Ladispoli lies in the environs of ancient Alsium. Based on archaeological remains, Ladispoli was a popular locus for coastal villas.
The modern Río Lérez on Spain's Atlantic coast.

Roman Lagentium (modern Castleford) is the site of a series of forts, beginning with a Flavian fort that was later replaced by a second-century fort. The site of the fort was occupied from ca. A.D. 80 to 150 while the vicus remained occupied until the fourth century.

The Lago di Massaciuccoli appears on Map 41 of the Barrington Atlas (grid square C2), but it is not named. In the introductory essay for Map 41 in the Map-by-Map Directory, W.V. Harris mentions the lake in the context of a brief discussion about the ancient hydrography of the territory around Pisa. Harris mentions that not only is there a need for more research about the ancient river courses, coa

A volcanic crater lake located near Viterbo, Italy. The study of lacustrine sediments has revealed palynological evidence that has helped to reconstruct the ancient environment and vegetation of peninsular Italy.
Large Roman military installation near present-day Wimborne Minster in Dorset. It was established very shortly after Claudian invasion (ca. 44 CE), and later served as a vexillation fortress.
Lakh-mazar is a toponym applied to gorges with rock-cut inscriptions located near Kuč, Iran.
Lakiadai was a deme of ancient Attica located on the Sacred Way between Sciron and the Cephissus.
Lalibela is an ancient site in in the Amhara Region of Ethiopia known especially for its 11 rock-cut churches.
An extensive villa, active between the first and sixth centuries of the modern era, located at modern Lamarque in the French commune of Castelculier (Nouvelle-Aquitaine).
Lamasba was a city of Roman Numidia.
A minor settlement, cited: BAtlas 34 D2 Lamsorti
Roman fort at present day Lancaster.

Modern Langon is a commune located in the Ille-et-Vilaine department of Brittany in northwestern France. Various archaeological remains from the Roman period survive there, including paved roads, the remains of a villa, and the so-called Chapelle Sainte-Agathe.
Laodikeia (Katakekaumene)/Claudiolaodicea was a Hellenistic city of central Anatolia established by built by Seleucus I Nicator.
The so-called "Large Palaestra" is an open square (ca. 140 x 140 m) surrounded by porticoes built in the early first century A.D.
The so-called "Large Theater" at Pompeii was built in the Greek style during the second century B.C. Its capacity was approximately 5,000 spectators.

A square in the Campus Martius of Rome, at the center of which lies an archaeological site that includes the remains of four temples of the Republican period, as well as elements of the first century B.C. theater complex of Cnaeus Pompeius.
An amphitheater of the first century A.D.
An ancient settlement located in mountainous terrain to the north of Tralleis.

An ancient fortified acropolis of Argos, located on the hill named Larisa, which is located to the northwest of the town. The site is now occupied by a Venetian castle that incorporates or covers architectural and archaeological remains dating from the Mycenaean period through the 19th century.
An ancient city of the Troad, located at modern Limantepe in Turkey.
Larymna was a settlement of ancient Caria. Its location roughly corresponds with Incirli Ada in Asiatic Turkey.
Cave network near Montignac, France with over 600 Upper Paleolithic wall paintings.
Final phase of a sacred space dedicated to the worship of the god Mithras at Dura-Europos.
The Lateran Obelisk is a monumental Egyptian obelisk, completed during the reign of Thutmose IV (ca. 1400 BCE) and looted from Karnak in the early fourth century CE.
Latmos M. (Beşparmak Mountains) run east-west along the north shore of the former Latmian Gulf on the coast of Caria.
Lato pros Kamara was the port of ancient Lato.
An ancient people, tribe, or cultural group. Located: Vallo di Lauro.

The Castellum Laurum along the frontier in Germania Inferior was built first in the AD 40s and then destroyed during the Batavian Revolt of AD 69. The rebuilt fort remained in use until the early fifth century.

Salvage excavations during the 1970s in modern Le Candéou, a neighborhood of Peymeinade (France), identified multiple Roman-era structures that have been interpreted as agricultural in nature, including facilities for processing olive oil.
BAtlas 11 F4 Le Châtelet de Gourzon
A Gallo-Roman site with a long history of occupation. There is evidence at Vézelay for the processing of iron ore, as well as a temple dedicated to Bacchus and a Gallo-Roman fanum.

The archaeological site at Le Peu (Charente) dates originally to the mid-fifth millennium BCE and preserves evidence of a fortified Middle Neolithic settlement with timber structures. The ditch and palisade fortifications and the timber structures represent the earliest evidence of such architecture in Atlantic Europe. The fortified site is located close to the monumental Tusson tumuli.
An Iron Age and Roman settlement located 1km southeast of Leaze Farm was identified through aerial photography and metal detection.
A Roman auxiliary fort on the Danube river at modern Ram (Serbia). It was reduced in size by the time of Diocletian and then renovated and expanded under Justinian.

Lees Hall Roman Camp is an archaeological site that was once an ancient Roman temporary camp located near Hadrian's Wall (Northumberland, England). Once there were more than 40 temporary Roman camps located near Hadrian's Wall.
A coastal village on the island of Euboea known especially for rich Bronze Age and Iron Age material.
An island of the Sporades mentioned by Pliny the Elder. The Barrington Atlas tentatively identified it with modern Ligada.
The Lekton promontory (modern Cape Baba or Baba Burnu) is the the westernmost point of Asia Minor.
Indigenous peoples of the Aegean littoral, mentioned in Classical and Hellenistic sources. Their historicity has been questioned.

A large volcanic island in the northern Aegean Sea. Lemnos appears frequently in Greek myth, not least as the crash-landing place of the god Hephaestos (Vulcan) when he was thrown from Mount Olympus by Zeus for attempting to protect his mother Hera.
The Lemovices were a Gaulish tribe centered around Augustoritum (Limoges).

The Lemovii were a Germanic tribe whose territory was close to that of the Rugii and the Gutones, all of which lie near the Vistula river delta. Tacitus mentions the tribe in his treatise on Germania.
Lepti Minus was an ancient port city in Tunisia.
This Roman theater in the modern French commune of Thénac was discovered in the 19th century. Its presence implies an ancient settlement or extra-urban sanctuary.
A Roman farm villa with extensive second-century CE Gallo-Roman mosaics, located at modern Les Près-Bas, just south of Loupian in Hérault, France. The site was occupied for more than 600 years.
A Roman fort and tower in the modern French commune of St-Gemmes-le-Robert (Pays de la Loire).
An ancient Gallo-Roman sanctuary near modern Genainville (France), with excavated remains of a temple, nymphaeum, and theater: BAtlas 11 B3 Génainville (sic)
At Lessa, Pausanias observed a sanctuary sacred to Athena where a wooden cult image was to be seen.
Lesura fl., a lefthand tributary of the Moselle river.
Letopolis was an ancient Egyptian city. It served as the capital of the second nome of Lower Egypt.
The ancient Ionian island of Leucas is known today as Lefkada.
The Leuci were an Iron Age Belgic tribe centered in the southern part of the modern Lorraine region.
Leucopetra Pr. (Punta di Pellaro) in Calabria is the extreme southwestern point of mainland Italy.
An island on the coast of Lucania.
Leukai was an ancient harbor city on the north shore of the Gulf of Smyrna.
Leukai was an ancient settlement of Laconia, located near the northeastern edge of the plain of Leuce.
Leuke, now Koufonísi, is a small, rocky island southeast of Crete that in antiquity was a center for the production of the purple dye derived from from the gastropod Murex trunculus.

Leuke Akte, the ‘White cape’ located on the Libyan coast of Egypt, was the site of an Isis cult wherein the Egyptian goddess was worshipped as Aphrodite, Muchis, and Eseremphis. An oracular shrine of Apollo was also found there.
Leukonoion was an Attic asty deme.
Leuktron was an ancient settlement in the southern Peloponnese. Pausanias places it twenty stades from Pephnus.
An ancient settlement, labeled on the Peutinger Map and listed by both the Antonine and Ravenna itineraries. Modern Mrkonjić Grad in Bosnia-Herzegovina.
The Lexovii were a Celtic people on the western banks of the lower Sequana river.
Li Schiavoni is the site of a fortified Messapic center that flourished in the mid-first millennium BCE.
A mountain range of northern Syria that is between the Mediterranean coastline and the Antilibanos mountains of the interior.
The Libicii? were a tribe of Cisalpine Gauls.
The Library of Celsus is a library and monumental tomb in Ephesus which was constructed ca. 110-120 CE.

The Library of Hadrian is located on the north side of the Athenian Acropolis, immediately to the north of the Roman Agora. The Roman emperor Hadrian built the complex in A.D. 131/2. It was subsequently destroyed during the Herulian sack of Athens in A.D. 267.

The modern name for a library built on the southeast corner of the Agora in Athens by Flavius Pantainos ca. 97-102 AD. It was demolished to make way for the Post-Herulian Wall in the late third century AD.
A royal mausoleum, dating to the second century BCE, located at ancient Thugga (modern Dougga in Tunisia).
A tribe of the Vindelici, dwelling on the banks of the river Licus.
Site of Roman bathhouse accompanying possible villa, mansio, or larger settlement, at Lickfold near Wiggonholt in West Sussex
A Roman villa located some 1.2 km NW of Liestal, in the territory of Augusta Raurica. The villa dates to the middle of the first century A.D. and was sacked ca. A.D. 259.
An ancient people, tribe, or cultural group. Located: Tartagine and Asco area.
A harbor constructed in Constantinople during the reign of Theodosius I; thirty-seven Byzantine-era shipwrecks have been excavated from the harbor site.

The Dacian Limes refers to a series of ramparts, fortifications, and forts along the frontiers of the Roman province of Dacia. This system originates in the early second century CE and includes several components: Limes Alutanus, Limes Porolissensis, Limes Transalutanus in Wallachia, so-called "Trajan's Walls", and the so-called "Constantine Wall".
An ancient (and modern) copper mining landscape in the modern Paphos district of western Cyprus.
The Limpopo River in southern Africa flows some 1,750 km and drains more than 415,000 square kilometers. It flows eastward from South Africa, through Mozambique, and drains into the Indian Ocean.
An ancient settlement located at modern Yuvalılar in the district of Finike, Antalya province, Turkey.
A late-Roman bridge, ancient name unknown, located near the ancient city of Limyra in modern Turkey.
Small Roman fort of Agricolan date in Scotland
An ancient people, tribe, or cultural group.
The Livenza river is a river of northern Italy that flows into the Adriatic Sea.
A river of what is today the Mediterranean littoral of France, mentioned in Roman sources. It may be the same as the modern Libron.
The island of Guernsey shows evidence for prehistoric habitation. During the Roman period, there is evidence of both settlement and trading activity.
An island in the Adriatic, known today as Ugljan/Ugliano.
The site of a Roman villa discovered ca. 1760 and excavated in 1930. It lies ca. 2.5 km SE of Chedworth Roman villa.
Lithinos Pyrgos (now Tashkurgan, Xinjiang in China (塔什库尔干镇)) was a settlement located along the Silk Road. During the Han Dynasty the site was a major center of the Kingdom of Puli (蒲犁).
The so-called "Little Palace at Knossos" lies some 200 m northwest of the main Minoan "palace" center and to the east of the Unexplored Mansion to which it was once linked.
Livy discusses Litubium, along with Clastidium, in book 32 of his history.

The Lobetanoi were a pre-Roman tribe of Iberia mentioned only once by Ptolemy. Their homeland is thought to have been located in the mountainous area near Albarracín in the southwest Province of Teruel.
A now unlocated site that was the center of the Lobetani in ancient Iberia.

An archaeological site in La Playa de la Calera on the south coast of the Isla de Lobos in the northeast Canary Islands that has produced Roman imperial pottery and evidence of Muricidae mollusk processing for purple dye extraction.

Ptolemy names the Longos river in his circumdescription of the island of Alouion (Albion). It is possibly to be identified with the modern Loch Linnhe, which is open to the sea on Scotland's west coast.
A Roman fort at present-day Lanchester.

A Pre-Roman Iron Age farmstead with a relatively short occupational history gave way to a Roman installation that was situated outside the confines of the first-century fort at Longthorpe near Peterborough. This installation was termed a "works-depot" by its excavators and shows evidence of both ceramic production and metalworking. The installation was likely established soon after the fort's own
Burial site in Armenia containing tombs dated to the Late Bronze-Early Iron Ages (22nd-5th centuries BCE).
Iberian settlement of La Loma del Escorial and necropolis of Los Nietos (Cartagena, Murcia, SPAIN).
A fortified Iberian site in use from ca. 750 B.C. to 325 B.C.

The archaeological site of Los Villares is located northeast of the town of Quintana del Marco, Spain, and lies in the plain of the Orbigo River. The Roman villa at the site dates between the first and the fifth centuries CE.
Lake Cerknica is a an intermittent lake in southwestern Slovenia.
An ancient people, tribe, or cultural group. Located: near Nossa Signore di Castro.
An ancient promontory listed in Ptolemy's Geography. Thought to be the modern Cap Begur on the so-called Costa Brava: a section of the Mediterranean coast of modern Spain (Catalunya).
An Attic deme located in the Kephisos valley to the west of Athens.
A settlement in Azania, located near modern Kato Lusi, that has been under excavation since the late 19th century.
An ancient people, tribe, or cultural group. Located: upper Jalón valley.
An ancient Oscan-speaking population of south Italy.
A Spanish village located in the south of the province of Córdoba that belonged to the kingdom of Alfonso X.
Lucentum was a Phoenician and then Roman settlement in Tarraconensis that was largely abandoned after the third century.
A castle originally built by Frederick II, Holy Roman Emperor in AD 1233.
A Roman villa located at Acquatraversa on the Via Cassia that is frequently attributed to Lucius Verus.
A mountain in the ager Sabinus.
A small lake near Lake Avernus, the modern Lucrino in Italy.
A sanctuary of Feronia located at a spring on the via Appia near Tarracina.
A gladiatorial training school adjacent to the Flavian Amphitheater in Rome. The structure is attested on the Severan marble plan of Rome.

Lugnano in Teverina is a comune located in the Province of Terni in the modern Italian region of Umbria. It lies about 60 km south of Perugia and 25 km west of Terni. Archaeological investigation has documented important examples of villa culture as well as Late Antique funereal evidence.
Luguvalium was a fortified Roman settlement in Britannia built around a Roman fort.
A cave located at the foot of the Palatine Hill in Rome in which the she-wolf was said to have been found suckling the twins, Romulus and Remus.
The Lusitani were an Indo-European people occupying the western portion of the Iberian peninsula.
Located in France's Burgundy region, the Luxeuil Abbey was founded ca. 585–590 by the Irish missionary Saint Columbanus.
A sanctuary of Apollo Lyceios in Athens, which served as the seat of Aristotle's Peripatetic school of philosophy founded in 335/4 BCE. The Lyceum was destroyed by Sulla in 86 BCE.
Mount Lykaion is located in Arcadia. As a sacred site, Lykaion is thought to be the birthplace of Zeus and the home of Pan. Parrhasian Apollo was worshipped on the eastern slopes.
An ancient river of Cyprus, identified with the modern Kouris/Kourris/Kuris, which is now dammed and canalized in its lower course. It empties into the ocean at modern Episkopi (ancient Kourion).
A city of Arcadia and home of the cult of Despoina
Remains of fortifications dating to the Late Roman period.
A fortified settlement on Cyprus dating to the thirteenth and twelfth centuries B.C.

A group of Gallo-Roman houses was identified on the banks of the Loire river in 1824, with some archaeological investigation in 1962-68. Associated finds date the site to the second century A.D. A Gallo-Roman villa was also identified at the site.
Macae, Libyan Tribe, cited: BAtlas 35 F3

A rock-cut Etrusco-Roman sanctuary sacred to Demeter that was discovered during rescue excavations in 2006 following looting activity. The sanctuary, set in a grove, remained in use until the second century A.D.
A province of the Roman empire, formed in the mid-second century BCE, becoming a senatorial province in the mid-first century CE.

The Macellum at Jerash was built in the early second century CE. The complex focuses on a limestone-paved octagonal courtyard. The area occupied by the complex was likely an insula in the previous century.
A macellum of Roman Puteoli. The discovery of a statue of Serapis at the site led to a misidentification of the building as a Serapeum.
A fortified hilltop palace in Jordan located southeast of the mouth of the Jordan river on the eastern side of the Dead Sea.

A modern city in the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh, Machilipatnam served as a major port on the Bay of Bengal, from the 16th through the 19th centuries. Some Roman coins and Mediterranean ceramics have been recovered in the area.
The Magra river of northern Italy.
A Numidian site that eventually became a Roman colony in the second century A.D.
Madaba has a long settlement history. During the Roman period the city was part of the Trajanic province of Arabia.
Madonna del Parto is a Christian church at Sutri, dating to the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries. The rock-cut sanctuary repurposes a Mithraeum dating to the first and second centuries.

A modern comune located in the territory of Rieti, Lazio. The Rieti Survey identified this as a likely Roman-period settlement covering more than 5 ha. Material evidence suggests occupation from ca. the sixth century B.C. until the sixth century A.D.
Maen Llia is a standing stone located in the Brecon Beacons, Wales.
Maeotis, known in antiquity as a lake, is the modern Sea of Azov and is the shallowest of the world's seas.
An ancient tribe located to the north of Dalmatia near the Dalmatian-Pannonian border.
A Roman fort at modern-day Burrow Walls, probably to be identified with the ancient toponym "Magis".
Magnis was an important market town of the Dobunni tribe.
The modern Nahr Bayrut in Lebanon.
A Roman fortlet located near Brough in eastern Cumbria (England).
An ancient people, tribe, or cultural group. Located: middle Strymon valley BUL/MAC.
The tallest in Arcadia, Mainalion is part of the Menalon mountain range of the Peloponnese.
An ancient settlement of Arcadia, abandoned by Pausanias' day. Probably to be located near Daria.
A well-preserved Roman temple built ca. 16 B.C. and dedicated to Caius and Lucius Caesar.
Majorca is the largest island in the Balearic Islands archipelago in the western Mediterranean Sea.

Thatta was the capital of three successive dynasties and later ruled by the Mughal emperors of Delhi. The expansive necropolis is thought to have grown around the fourteenth-century shrine of Muhammad Hussain Abro.
Remains of a Hellenistic stoa initially identified via salvage excavation in the 1960s and further explored ca. 2012. J. Travlos identified the remains as those of the Palladion court.
A pre-Roman people settled in north-eastern Corsica (modern Casinca), mentioned by Ptolemy.
A promontory/peninsula on the eastern end of Sicily.
The modern Guadalmedina river, which debouches into the Mediterranean at modern Malaga, Spain (ancient Malaca)
The Isle of Mull is the second largest island of the Inner Hebrides, located off the west coast of Scotland.
A sacred structure with an 'in antis' plan located near Arzachena in Sardinia.
Cape Maleas is a cape located in the southeast of the Peloponnese.
A group of 10 major volcanic islands located in the Red Sea.
Site located south of the Theban Necropolis containing a New Kingdom palace complex constructed by Amenhotep III of the 18th Dynasty.
An ancient Indian tribe settled in the Punjab region at the time of Alexander's invasion.
The Maltepe tumulus at Pergamon is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site "Pergamon and its Multi-Layered Cultural Landscape".
The Manganello Sanctuary is located at the northern edge Caere's urban plateau.
The Hvar Channel is located between the islands of Brač and Hvar in the Adriatic Sea.
The ancient Marathoussa island is probably to be associated with the modern Yassıca Ada.
A Spanish village located in the east of the province of Sevilla that belonged to the kingdom of Alfonso X.
Marcomagus was a road station along the Roman road from Augusta Treverorum to Colonia Agrippinensis, the modern Nettersheim-Marmagen.
Early and Middle Bronze Age city in northern Mesopotamia.
An ancient people, tribe, or cultural group. Located: in plains of Saray; and in district of upper Kara Su to N?.
The Marduk Gate is one of Babylon's eight city gates and it is situated on the eastern side of the inner city, directly east of the Kullab quarter. King Nebuchadnezzar II built the gate ca. 575 B.C.
A brackish lake of Lower Egypt (now Lake Mariout).
Remains of a large religious complex, consisting of a fanum, two small subsidiary structures, and three altars.
A southern promontory of Corsica (modern Capo di Feno).
Marina di S. Nicola is located close to Alsium.
A Mithraic shrine of unusual size discovered at modern Marino, Italy in 1963.
A Judean, Edomite, and later Hellenistic settlement. Destroyed ca. 40 BCE by the Parthians.
Known today as Kayalı Dağ, this mountain is located in the modern Turkish province of Çanakkale.
Burial site in northern Iran containing over fifty burials dated to the mid-2nd millennium BCE.

The Domus Marmeniae is a villa located on the Via Appia near the fourth milestone. The villa grounds hosted a pagan necropolis and tradition holds that the matrona, Marmenia, relocated the body of St. Urban to a mausoleum built on the grounds.

The Marmoutier Abbey located near Tours, Indre-et-Loire, France is also known as the Abbey of Marmoutier or Marmoutiers. Saint Martin of Tours (316-397) founded the abbey in 372 after he became Bishop of Tours in 371.
Gurgum (kingdom) became an Assyrian province after Sargon II captured its capital Marqasi in 711 BC.

The Marrucini were an Italic tribe centered around Teate in the Abruzzo. In conflict with Rome through the end of the Second Samnite War, the Marrucini became allied with Rome thereafter. Their language was likely in the Sabellic family.
The Marsi were an ancient Italic tribe. Their chief center was located at Marruvium.
An ancient settlement at modern Slavonski Brod in Croatia.
A small stream (modern Dinar Su) that is a right tributary of the Maeander, just north of ancient Apamea/Kelainai/Kobotos (modern Dinar) in Turkey's Afyonkarahisar province.
The Marta river flows from Lake Bolsena to the Tyrrhenian Sea. Its course flows past both Tuscania and Tarquinia and enters the Tyrrhenian Sea near Lido di Tarquinia.

The Roman Tetrakionion at Aphrodisias has been identified as a Martyrion. Its date of construction is uncertain, ranging from as early as the late second century CE to as late as the 5th-6th century CE.
The Gallo-Roman sanctuary with twin temples was discovered in 1964 at the locality called Masamas in the commune of Saint-Léomer.
The Massa River of southern Morocco.
A major settlement, cited: BAtlas 34 F2 Mascula Tiberia
A place from the TAVO Index

The Roman-period remains at Massaciuccoli, including luxury villas, baths, and productive areas, are connected with the influential Venulei family. Perhaps of Etruscan origins, the Venulei are also to be linked with Pisa.
A Roman villa with an associated bath complex destroyed by the AD 79 eruption of Vesuvius, the Masseria De Carolis site is located in the comune of Pollena Trocchia near Naples, Italy.
Mons Massicus, a mountain ridge of ancient Italy, in the territory of the Aurunci, at the border of Latium and Campania.
A confederation of Berber tribes living in Numidia.
The site of the burial of Shepseskaf, the last known pharaoh of the Fourth Dynasty of Ancient Egypt.
BAtlas 47 E4 Mastro Paolo di Barrafranca
A modern city of Sri Lanka whence a hoard of ancient coins (now in the British museum) that included locally minted, late Roman imitations.
A mountain of the Peloponnese mentioned by Pausanias. Modern Lykodemos.
Matilo was a castellum along the Roman frontier system (limes) of Germania Inferior. It is located within present-day Leiden.
A town mentioned in Neo-Assyrian sources that is identified with modern Midyat. Midyat originated as a Hurrian settlement in the third millennium B.C.
A sanctuary that includes a Punic temple built in white limestone, a nuraghe, and a sacred well.

A late Roman province within the diocese of Africa. Mauretania Sitifensis was included on Map 101 of the Barrington Atlas ("Dioceses and Provinces of the Roman Empire") that follows the Verona List (ca. A.D. 303–324). Diocletian created the province and Constantine assigned it to the administrative Diocese of Africa. The Vandals conquered Mauretania Sitifensis and following the collapse of the Wes
A Roman mausoleum dating most likely to the second century.
A Roman tomb located in the archaeological area of Casinum that dates to either the first or second centuries CE.
Mausoleum and Sacred area of Hecatomnus
A mausoleum and sacred precinct associated with Hecatomnus of Mylasa, who was the satrap of Caria under Artaxerxes II (404–358 BC).

The Mausoleum at Halicarnassus is a tomb built between 353 and 350 B.C. for Mausolus, a satrap in the Persian Empire. Antipater of Sidon identified it as one of his Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.

A tomb on the Via Appia south of Rome belonging to Caecilia Metella, a daughter of Metellus Creticus. She was born ca. 100 BC. In 1303, the tomb was incorporated into the Castrum Caetani, serving as the main tower of the fortification.
A mausoleum built to entomb Diocletian at his retirement palace that was constructed around 295 CE and is located in modern day Split, Croatia.
A mausoleum on the Via Appia that has been identified conventionally as that of the emperor Gallienus.
A tumulus-type tomb discovered in 1887 belonging to the military tribune M. Lucilius Paetus of the gens Lucilia.
A Roman mausoleum that is associated with Lucius Munatius Plancus.
The so-called mausoleum of Menenius Agrippa stands along the Via Nomentana.
Tomb of Valerius Romulus (ca. AD 292/295 – 309), son of Maxentius, along the Via Appia.

A monument built in Ravenna, Italy, ca. AD 520 by Theodoric the Great as his future tomb. After Belisarius reconquered Ravenna in 540, the tomb was converted into the church of Sta. Maria della Rotonda.
An extensive archaic necropolis located on the eastern edge of modern Mavişehir in Turkey, which was associated with ancient Panormos, the port of Didyma.

Ruins of a villa complex at modern Les Mazieres in the French commune of Gourdon-Murat with associated funerary monument, pond, and other components. The site was discovered and excavated in the 20th century. Its ancient name is unknown.

Mazzorbo is an island in the Venetian Lagoon. It is sparsely populated in the present day. In antiquity, it may have received displaced persons from Altinum following its sacking in the fifth century CE.
A place from the TAVO Index

Nineveh's western wall had seven (or eight) gates: the Mašqû Gate was the northernmost one. The Neo-Assyrian king Sennacherib constructed it and gave it the Akkadian ceremonial name Ea-mušēšir-kuppīya, which means "The God Ea Is the One Who Properly Directs (Water Flow into) My Cisterns."
Roman sanctuary with two small temples.

Ancient Mediana, also referred to as the Gnotzheim fort, was a Roman military camp that was part of Upper Germanic-Raetian Limes. The site is located on what is now agricultural land in the Weißenburg-Gunzenhausen district of Bavaria.
The Caliphate City of Medina Azahara is a city built in the mid-tenth century CE by the Umayyad dynasty as the seat of the Caliphate of Cordoba.
The Medina of Essaouira, formerly Mogador, is a late eighteenth-century fortified town with ancient Phoenician origins. It is located on the Atlantic coast of Morocco.
A Roman fort and town located between Deva Victrix (Chester) and Viroconium Cornoviorum (Wroxeter).
Mega Helos, a wetland in Attica located northeast of the Plain of Marathon.

Ptolemy enumerates the ancient mouths (stomata) of the Ganges river, from west to east. He lists "Mega Stoma" as the second of these. Due to significant natural and constructed changes in the hydrology of the Ganges within and since antiquity, modern scholars cannot securely identify a particular channel in the Ganges delta today, but the Barrington Atlas does connect the ancient Oxymatis (modern

Megali Koryfi, an archaeological site on the island of Aegina in proximity to the Christian chapel of Ag. Antonios that is noted for the presence of substantial remains of drystone fortifications dating to the Mycenaean period.
A Middle to Late Bronze Age settlement located on the hill of Megali Magoula that includes Mycenaean chamber tombs.
An ancient settlement in Arcadia in the Peloponnese, likely founded in the 4th century BCE. The site lies just to the northeast of the modern town of Megalopolis.
Megaron A is an apsidal megaron built sometime between 1400 BC and 1100 BC in the area of the later Sanctuary of Apollo at Thermon.
Megiste Ins. (modern Kastellorizo) is the easternmost Greek island. In antiquity, it was colonized by Dorian Greeks.
Meidum is located in the desert south of Cairo and is the site of numerous mudbrick mastabas and a pyramid.
Meinarti Island is located in the Nile River north of the Second Cataract. It lies just upstream of the Sudanese border town of Wadi Halfa.
A river that flows into the Black Sea: the modern Melet in northern Turkey.
The island of Malta, located in the Mediterranean Sea between Sicily and Libya.
Melite was a deme of ancient Attica. It was located in the urban center of Athens and included both the Agora and the Pnyx. It belonged to the tribe of Kekropis.
A river of Lucania that flows into the Tyrrhenian Sea.
The Melfa River flows through Lazio, originating from the Monti della Meta and joining the Liri River near San Giovanni Incarico.
An ancient people whose territory is unlocated
A Belgic tribe of northern Gaul.
The third eastern-most ancient mouth of the Nile River.
An ancient Greek sanctuary of Helen and Menelaos near ancient Therapnai in Greece.
Meninx/Lotophagitis/Girba Ins. (modern Djerba) is the largest island of North Africa.
Ancient Menouthis was sacred to both Isis and Serapis. Its ruins are now submerged.
An ancient city placed in the Gargano and discussed by Pliny the Elder.
Probably to be identified with Tirich Mir, the highest mountain of the Hindu Kush mountain range.
The Messapii were an ancient Indo-European people occupying the Salento peninsula in southeast Italy.
A small mountain range that is located in the northeastern part of Boeotia and mainland Euboea. This mountain range borders the North Euboean Gulf and the Euripus Strait.

The so-called "Meta Romuli" was a pyramidal tomb located in the Ager Vaticanus in Rome. It likely dates to the first century BCE or the first century CE. Its extant superstructure was demolished in 1499. Remains of foundations and pavements that have been associated with the tomb were encountered in 1948-1949 during construction work in the first block of the north side of the present-day Via dell

A large fountain located southwest of the Flavian Amphitheater and completed under Domitian (ca. A.D. 96). Four of Rome's Augustan regions converged at this point (I, III, IV, X); it is possible that Regio II also intersected the other four regiones at this place.
Metagonium Promontorium may be the modern-day Cap Bougaroûn. It is a cape that forms the western end of the Gulf of Skikda. It lies opposite the Cap de Fer and is the northernmost point of Algeria.

A Roman fort built in the area of modern Birmingham, England, soon after the Roman invasion of A.D. 43. The fort, about 200 square meters in area, was in use periodically until its abandonment ca. A.D. 120.
Temple at Olympia constructed in the late 4th or early 3rd century BCE
Metropolis was a city located in southern Phrygia.
One of two gates providing access from the west through the southern end of the citadel defense walls at Dura-Europos.

The Middle Stoa, the largest structure in the Agora of Athens, was built after 183 BC, as the north side of the South Square. In the Augustan Period, the Odeon of Agrippa was built on its north side. It was destroyed during the Herulian Sack of 267 AD and used as building material for the Post-Herulian Wall.
A large Neolithic chambered cairn located on the island of Rousay, Orkney, Scotland.

Mikro Kameni is a non-extant island that was formed in the Santorini caldera some time before 1851, when it was attested in the Admiralty Chart of Robert Graves, HMS Volgae. It was joined to Nea Kameni at some point after this, probably in the major period of volcanic activity in 1866-1870.
One of the milecastles along Hadrian's Wall, approximately 400 meters to the west of Housesteads Roman fort (Vercovicium)
A milecastle situated on Hadrian's Wall.
A milecastle situated on Hadrian's Wall.
A milecastle situated on Hadrian's Wall.
A milecastle situated on Hadrian's Wall.
Milefortlet 1 (Biglands House) of the Roman Cumbrian Coast defences.
A freshwater lake in the vicinity of Bursa, Turkey.
Intramural military base located on the north and east side of Dura-Europos.
Intramuros military assembly and training ground on the eastern side of Dura-Europos.
Military compound in the Temple of Artemis Azzanathkona
A complex of rooms requisitioned for military record keeping and administration, formerly belonging to the Temple of Artemis Azzanathkona.
The Minaei were an ancient people of Yemen, numbered by Strabo as one of the four great nations of the southern Arabian peninsula.
The Mincio river is a tributary of the Po river.
Minerva temple at Punta della Campanella
An ancient temple of Minerva, located on the ancient cape that also was known by the goddess' name.
The Minervae promunturium is identified by modern scholars with the Punta Campanella, which lies at the western extremity of the Sorrentine Peninsula.
Multi-period mining, principally for turquoise, but also for other minerals, was carried out on the Serabit el-Kahdim plateau in the Sinai (modern Egypt).
A river that flows some 62 km from the Monti Sabatini to the Tyrrhenian Sea. The modern Mignone.
A city of the Indo-Scythian kingdom, located on the Indus river in modern Pakistan, upstream of Barygaza.
Minorca is one of the Balearic Islands of the Mediterranean Sea. Its name likely derives from the Latin 'Insula minor'.

Minori is the site of a major villa located on the Amalfi coast, some 11 km WSW of Salerno. Destroyed by a possible landslide, the villa was in use from the Iulio-Claudian period through to the Flavian period.
Cemetery site in Northern Egypt with burials from the predynastic period as well as the late Roman period.
The remains of an Archaic period structure at Mira Lanza, located in Via Luigi Pierantoni.
A celtiberian and subsequent Roman settlement at modern Ciudad Rodrigo in Salamanca, Spain.
A Roman fort occupied ca. 70-85 CE in Wales.
A river that flows from just south of Arcevia to the Adriatic Sea. The Nevola river joined the Misa before it drains into the sea near Senigallia.
A place from the TAVO Index
A well-preserved Mithraeum with modern stone vault above ground and site below in Fertőrákos, Hungary, at the site of ancient Scarbantia.
A mithraeum was excavated at Segontium (modern Caernarfon) in 1959, ca. 137m from the east corner of the Roman auxiliary fort. The site was abandoned in the late fourth century A.D.
A temple sacred to Mithras located at the Roman fort of Vindovala (Rudchester) on Hadrian's Wall.

A mithraeum was discovered at Vulci in 1975 during excavations of a Roman aristocratic house. The shrine was well preserved with two tauroctony scenes dating to the third century. The site was destroyed in the fourth century A.D.
The Mithraeum of Lucretius Menander located in ancient Ostia dates to the third century CE.
The so-called Mithraeum of the Seven Gates was built at Ostia in the second century CE, repurposing rooms that originally date to the previous century.
The so-called Mithraeum of the Seven Spheres is located in ancient Ostia near to the theater-cum-quadriporticus complex. The so-called Quattro tempietti screen it from the Decumanus Maximus.
Megalithic temple complex of the fourth millennium BC.
The Mokvi river flows from the southern slopes of the Kodori Range to the Black Sea.
Mochlos is an island in the Gulf of Mirabello, although in antiquity it was likely connected to the Cretan mainland. The island is the site of an ancient Minoan settlement.

Buddhist cave monastery complex in the cliffs above the Dachuan River near the Dunhaung Oasis, constructed in 366 CE and in use until the 14th Century CE. The caves contain thousands of murals and painted sculptures, and thousands of manuscripts in Chinese, Tibetan, Uyghur, Sogdian, Sanskrit, and Khotanese were stored in the so-called "Library Cave." The Mogao Caves were added to UNESCO's World He
Burial site in the Minusinsk Basin (southern Siberia) containing over 50 burials dated to the 1st millennium BCE.
Mokha, a port city on the Red Sea, is a key trading center that reaches its peak in the seventeenth century. It succeeds the ancient Mouza Emporion.
An ancient settlement 30 km north of Rome that was excavated from 1986-90. An imperial villa existed on the site up until the third century AD.

Fortified settlement located near the modern village of Smolenice, Slovakia containing signs of habitation from the Eneolithic period through the Middle Ages, with an apparent peak during the Halstatt period.
San Pietro di Tolve Roman villa.
Monastery of Saint John the Theologian
The Monastery of Saint John the Theologian (also known as the Monastery of Saint John the Divine) is a Greek Orthodox monastery dating to AD 1088 on the island of Patmos.
Monastery of Simeon Stylites the Younger
A sixth-century AD monastery named for Simeon Stylites the Younger who lived atop a pillar on Thaumaston Oros.
A Medieval refuge settlement founded ca. AD 583 that developed into an important center from the tenth century onward.
A mountain (modern Jabal Faţīrah in the Egypt's eastern desert). Site of Roman-era mining and military activities.
A mountain range; BAtlas 20 lists it as unlocated but near either Moslavačka gora or Ivančica, Croatia.
Mons Seleucus was the site of the famous battle between Constantius II and the usurper Magnentius in AD 353. The Gallo-Roman vicus at La Bâtie-Montsaléon included a Gallo-Roman sanctuary.
A massif that was the site of human settlement from prehistoric times onward.
A series of noncontinuous fortifications are extant on Mount Gildone (elevation 902 meters) that enclose part of an upland plateau. A nucleus of 23 Samnite tombs was also discovered in the vicinity.
A Sikel center located on a calcareous hill (560 m). There is evidence of rock-cut chamber tombs dating to the archaic period.

The tumulus of Montariolo originally measured some 4 meters in height and 50 meters in diameter. It included more than 350 tombs. It was used during several phases, stretching from the ninth to the fifth centuries BCE.
Monte Aguzzo di Formello (Rome), the site of a tumulus along the road leading for Veii to the Ager Faliscus.
BAtlas 47 E3 Monte Balzo di Alimena
Monte Bernorio is the site of a fortified Cantabrian settlement covering more than 120 hectares.

The remains of a Roman villa that belonged to the family of the Bruttii Praesentes were found in the locality known as 'Madonna dei Colori' near the ancient road station Vicus Novus/Ad Novas, modern Osteria Nuova, some 53 km northeast of Rome.
BAtlas 47 D3 Monte Falcone di Baucina
A peak of the Tuscan-Romagnolo Apennines, rising to 1,654 m. above sea level, Monte Falterona is the source of the Arno River and shows evidence of Etruscan occupation.
A Faliscan sanctuary located on the slopes of Monte Li Santi.
BAtlas 44 F3 Monte Monaco di Gioia

The sanctuary of Monte Papalucio was an important Messapian sanctuary. It is located on the mountain of the same name in the territory of Oria in the province of Brindisi. The deities Demeter and Persephone were venerated in this cave sanctuary.
Monte Rovello was an important Etruscan settlement covering ca. 5 hectares with occupation stretching from the Bronze Age to the Hellenistic period.
The remains of a multi-period pre-Roman and Roman sanctuary.
At Monte Vairano are the remains of a fortified center of the Pentrian Samnites.
A ramped, megalithic structure in Sardinia dated to around 2700-2000 BC.

Monte del Grano is a popular name that was assigned to a mausoleum once thought to belong to Alexander Severus, although that assignation is no longer supported. The archaeological remains are now part of the Parco XVII Aprile 1944.
A Talayotic settlement of the early first millennium BCE.
An Etruscan settlement in proximity to the course of the Arno river that was active from the fifth to the first centuries B.C.
A Medieval settlement where numerous important Etruscan tombs have been excavated.
The Monterozzi necropolis is an Etruscan necropolis located to the east of Tarquinia. The necropolis contains about 6,000 graves.
A hilltop settlement with a long-term habitation, stretching from ca. 2000 BC to the first century BC. The archaeological site preserves the remains of 4+ mid-first millennium BC dwellings.

The hill of Monteverde, a part of the Ianiculum hill to the west of the Tiber river, was a source of a brown, lithoid tuff (tufo di Monteverde) that was quarried for use as a building material from the second century BC.
BAtlas 47 C3 Montevergine di S. Anna
Monti della Tolfa, a volcanic group of mountains in the Anti-Apennines in the northern part of Lazio in central Italy.

Ashby describes the area of the Vigna Montioni as the findspot of numerous funereal inscriptions and funerary altars. This vineyard of the early twentieth century seems likely to have been the location of the villa of the Iavoleni.
The modern Montone river (southwest of Ravenna) was probably known by the ancient name Vitis.
This monumental complex of buildings at the city of Gabii was likely constructed in the mid-third century BCE as a public area for feasts, bathing, and ritual activities.
A first millennium B.C. ringfort in County Clare, Ireland, with three concentric rings of fortifications. At 27 acres, this is one of the largest hill forts in Iron Age Europe.
The House of Ganymede at Morgantina is a peristyle house with mosaic floor pavements. The earliest phase of the house belongs to the third century B.C.
Morginnum (Moirans) was a settlement of Gallia Narbonensis, along the road from Vienne to Alpis Cottia.
An extensive ancient site in northwest Cyprus occupied from the Bronze Age until approximately 700 B.C.
The Morsynos river (modern Dandalaz Çayı in Turkey) is a tributary of the Maeander river.
Mortuary temple of the Nineteenth Dynasty in the Theban Necropolis.
The New Kingdom period Mortuary Temple of Ramesses III at Medinet Habu.
The modern "Dead Sea", which is bordered by Israel, Jordan, and the West Bank.
An ancient population of Asia Minor. The Greeks used the term Mossynoikoi meaning "dwellers in wooden towers" to describe them.
A hill located near the acropolis of Athens. Pausanias discusses fortifications in the Hellenistic period; later the Philopappos Monument was built at the summit.

A place mentioned in passing in the Vita of Saint Desiderius. Modern scholars have identified it with modern Moissac in southern France where there are significant Merovingian and later medieval remains, some of which overlie structures of late Roman date.

Burial ground with 25 graves in 11 mounds located 10km Northeast of Manych, Kalmykia. These graves are largely from the Bronze Age and early Copper Age with some early Iron Age and Medieval graves also present.

Muggia's beginnings as a prehistoric fortified village (castelliere) came ca. the eighth and seventh centuries B.C. This territory came under Roman control in the 170s BC. In 931, king Hugh of Italy donated Muggia to the Patriarch of Aquileia.

Cave tomb near the modern village of Silat aḑ-Ḑahr containing burials from the Roman and Byzantine periods (1st-early 7th century CE). The cave is named after the Abu Halimeh family, which owned the land on which the cave is located at the time of its excavation in 1949.
A mountain peak Mulhacén, rises to 3,479 m (11,414 ft), making it the highest mountain of the Iberian Peninsula. It is part of the Sierra Nevada range in the Cordillera Penibética.

Munda, in southern Iberia, was the site of two important battles in antiquity. The first was Cn. Cornelius Scipio's defeated of the Carthaginians in 214 B.C. and the second Iulius Caesar's victory over the Pompeians in 45 B.C.
Munda fl. (Mondego River) is a river of Lusitania.
Mundigak is an archaeological site in Afghanistan's Kandahar province where evidence for a 'palace' belonging to the Harappan transitional phase has been discovered.
An ancient city whose site is now known as Henchir-Zouitina in modern Tunisia.
A hill in the Piraeus and the site of extensive fortifications in the Classical and Hellenistic periods.
The so-called "Mura Greche" are remains of the later third-century B.C. fortifications of Neapolis.
A second century A.D. Roman villa built atop an earlier villa rustica.

Muradiye (Armenian: Berkri) is a modern settlement in the Van Province in the southeast of Turkey. Here a fragmentary stele with an inscription (CTU A 5-16) of the Urartian king Minua (9th / 8th century BCE) has been found, which reports the construction of the "Canal of Minua" that is still in use today. The stela is now lost and its exact findspot is unknown.
Remains of third-century BCE fortifications that belong to Cartagena's Punic phase.
The Roman walls of León date initially from 74 CE. They are used and augmented after antiquity through the Middle Ages.

A Spanish castle and village located in the north of the province of Córdoba that belonged to the kingdom of Alfonso X. Today it's known as Castillo de Murgabal or Castillo de Almogábar. It is part of the village of Torrecampo and the region of Fuencaliente.
The site of a Neolithic village located in the territory of Matera in southern Italy. The site was initially discovered in the 1890s by Domenico Ridola.
The Republican city wall of Rome.
An early earthwork at Rome described by Varro, the Murus Terreus may have been part of the so-called Servian Wall. It was likely located on the Oppian Hill, between the Subura and the Carinae.
The settlement of Mut el-Kharab, located in Egypt's Dakhleh Oasis. A temple to the god Seth was built at this location.
An important port and trading village
A town mentioned in Neo-Assyrian sources. Although the city's exact location is not known, it has tentatively been identified with modern Mergasur, which is 10 km west of Topzawa.

A shaft well nearly forty metres deep on the north side of the Acropolis of Athens, opened up around 1200 BC to provide a water supply for the citadel. It was abandoned after the upper staircase collapsed around 1175 BC and filled with rubbish. The entrance is near the northwest corner of the house of the Arrhephoroi.

Mycenaean burial ground located approximately 8 kilometers west of Nemea containing 20 tombs dated to the 15th century BCE. All but two of the burials were looted in the 1970s, but the illicit finds were retrieved and repatriated to Greece in 1996.
An ancient settlement on Crete, probably to be located at Kastelli: Selli.
An ancient people who lived on the Arabian peninsula south of the Strait of Hormuz, and who may have been Persian subjects.
Myriand(r)os was an ancient Phoenician port near modern İskenderun, Turkey.
Myrtoion Mare (Myrtoan Sea) is a part of the Mediterranean Sea lying between the Cyclades and the Peloponnese.
A fortress in Thrace, whose precise location is now unknown.
An ancient lake in Akarnania, the modern Limni Voulkaria.

A burial area on the Black Sea coast that is associated with the settlement of Myskhako. In 1978-1979 excavations were conducted that uncovered 81 burial sites dating to the Bronze Age, the Classical period, and the Middle Ages.
A fortified town in Laconia, Peloponnese, Greece, Mystras was named as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1989.

An ancient dam, subsequently reused, repaired, and adapted into modern times, in the Glosses pass east of Alyzeia (modern Kalima) and just below the later site of the Byzantine fortress of Varnako/Barnako. Remains of aqueduct and mill fittings of various dates have been noted; the dam and its reservoir are presumed to have been created originally (perhaps in Classical or Hellenistic times) to supp
An ancient people, tribe, or cultural group. Located: area of Oued Sebaou.

A major modern reservoir in Sri Lanka, located southeast of Anuradhapura. Its original construction is traditionally dated to the late third or early fourth century CE. BAtlas 5 inset labels its geometry as "Megisba Stagnum", a toponym for a swamp or wetland reported by Pliny during the first century CE.
Nagarjunakonda was a Buddhist archaeological site located in Andhra Pradesh, India.
According to Pliny, Nagia was the largest center of the Gebanitae in southern Arabia.
Cave site located on the banks of Nahal Hemar in the southern Judean Desert. The site contains traces of habitation dated to the pre-pottery Neolithic (ca. 6900-6300 BCE).
Cave in western Samaria containing archaeological traces from the Pottery Neolithic period (Yarmukian culture), the Chalcolithic Period, and the Early Bronze Age.
Over twenty rock reliefs (with accompanying inscriptions) are carved into the limestone cliffs around the estuary of the Nahr al-Kalb river.
A Sasanian irrigation system in central Iraq, associated with the Tigris and Diyala rivers. It seems to have been created in the 6th century CE and remained in use into the 10th.
The modern Narmada River in Gujarat, India, originates in the Vindhya mountain range and flows west to empty into the Gulf of Khambhat.
A Gallic people on the west coast of Gallia Lugdunensis, on the north bank of the Liger river.
The Nantuates were a Celtic people dwelling in the upper Rhône valley. They formed part of the confederation known as "quattuor civitates Poeninae".
An ancient necropolis located northwest of Persepolis.

Narekavank, or Narek Monastery, was a tenth-century Armenian monastery near the southern shore of Lake Van. It was a major monastic center, and the mystical poet Grigor Narekatsi (951-1003) studied and resided there. The monastery was abandoned and demolished in the 20th century.
An ancient island, likely to be identified with the modern Sfyrna island located off the northwest coast of Rhodes.
The Nasamones were a nomadic tribe of northern Libya.
An inland city of Arabia Felix.
Naveta de Son Morell de Dalt
A prehistoric funerary monument located in the municipality of Ciutadella, on the island of Menorca, España.
A chamber tomb of the late second to early first millennium BCE located on the island of Minorca.

Navio, located near modern Brough, was a Roman fort of Flavian origin that was abandoned ca. A.D. 120. By 154 it has been rebuilt with a different orientation. There is evidence of continued use in the third and fourth centuries.
Nazzano Romano was the site of an Etruscan settlement covering some 7 hectares and dating between the eighth and fifth centuries B.C.
Nea Nikomedeia is a Neolithic settlement in Macedonia, dating to the seventh millennium BC.
Neapolis (modern Nabeul, Tunisia) is a coastal town on the Cap Bon peninsula that was founded by Greeks from Cyrene in the fifth century B.C.
An important Scythian settlement, capital of the late Scythian state on the Crimean peninsula.
An ancient settlement on the Adriatic coast. Modern Novigrad in Croatia.
Neapolis Theodorias was a Roman and Byzantine city in Cyrenaica. It was re-founded in AD 539 by Theodora after it was destroyed by the Vandals.
Nebelivka is a Neolithic-period archaeological site in Ukraine.
The modern Rio Neiva in Portugal.
Nebrodes M. are a major mountain range on the island of Sicily.

Two rock reliefs with inscriptions of the Neo-Babylonian king Nebuchadnezzar II were engraved in the Wadi esh-Sharbin, about 2 km southwest of the modern Lebanese town Brissa (also called Braïssé, Brisa).
The Cappella necropolis preserves a complex of underground tombs arranged along the ancient road connecting Misenum and Cumae. The earliest tombs date to the late first century BCE.
A Hellenistic and Roman period necropolis located in Messina, Sicily, in the area now referred to as "Orti della Maddalena".
The Fusco necropolis is the largest and oldest burial area in Greek Syracuse. Located within contrada Canalicchio, the site was excavated by Paolo Orsi in 1893.
A large Roman necropolis in Messina, uncovered in 1914 during the works to build the modern Palazzo della Prefettura.
The Necropolis of Mesu ‘e Montes contains at least 18 tombs of the domus de janas type. The necropolis dates from the later Neolithic period to the middle Bronze Age.
The Necropolis of Montessu is located near Villaperuccio, Sardinia. It is the site of about 40 domus de Janas tombs and dates to the third millennium B.C.
A large, rock-cut necropolis of over 5,000 tombs dating from the thirteenth to the seventh centuries BC.
A pre-Roman and Roman period necropolis on the outskirts of Teramo.
The Porta Ercolano necropolis, excavated between 1763 and 1838, is the best known of Pompeii's necropoleis, in use from the middle of the first century BC until the first century AD.
Burial ground containing 28 burials dated to the Etruscan period.
A prehistoric necropolis in Sardinia associated with the Ozieri culture and dating to the Final Neolithic period (ca. 3500-2900 BC).
A prehistoric necropolis at Porto Torres, Sardinia, containing at least 22 domus de ianas type tombs.
A river of Greece, rising on the slopes of Mt. Lykaion and flowing west to empty into the Gulf of Kyparissia just south of the modern village of Giannitsochori.
Gsell AAA (whence BAtlas) noted remains of a Roman settlement on the plateau of Nekmaria at a place then known as Djebel Kerkour.
An ancient sanctuary of necromancy sacred to Hades and Persephone located on the banks of the Acheron River in Epirus, near the ancient city of Ephyra.
Nelcynda was located some fifty miles from Muziris in the kingdom of the Pandyas.
Today an intermittent drainage known as the Nemeas or Zapantis that rises in the vicinity of ancient Nemea and flows north, emptying into the Corinthian Gulf near the modern village of Vrachati.

Nemorensis Lacus (modern Lake Nemi) is a small, volcanic lake in Latium located south of Rome. The lake is known for its adjacent sanctuary of the goddess Diana and for the recovery of several sunken Roman ships of the first century AD.
The site of a Roman villa some 40 km upstream on the Moselle from Trier. The site was discovered in 1852 and was excavated between 1866 and 1876.
Nertobriga Concordia Iulia was a Roman municipium.
Belgic tribes of northern Gaul at the time of its conquest by Rome. Their territory corresponds to the central part of modern Belgium.
Nesactium was an ancient town of Histria.

The Nesiotic league (the League of the Islanders) was a federal organization of Greek poleis in the Cyclades islands, organized in ca.  314/3 BCE under the direction of Antigonus Monophthalmus. Control passed to the Ptolemies ca. 287 BCE; the league eventually dissolved in the mid-3rd century BCE.
Nesis? fl., a river of the western Caucasus flowing into the Black Sea.
The modern Boğsak Islet in Turkey's Mersin Province.
An ancient fortified settlement in Arcadia.
An ancient river in the general vicinity of Akragas on the island of Sicily, the Nestis is possibly to be identified with the modern Torrente Iacono.
A Roman fort site at Nether Denton that was identified via cropmarks. The fort formed part of the Stanegate frontier system, and thus pre-dates Hadrian's Wall. It was abandoned ca. 122.
A significant cult center at Nettleton Shrub in Wiltshire was dedicated to Apollo Cunomaglus.
A basilica in Ravenna, Italy, erected by Theodoric the Great in the first quarter of the sixth century AD.

New Kalabsha is a promontory located near Aswan. It currently is the site of several ancient temples relocated to avoid the rising waters of Lake Nasser created by the construction of the Aswan High Dam.
An ancient people, tribe, or cultural group. Located: near Tigisis/Hodna.
The modern La Nied river, a tributary of the Saar, which runs through parts of modern France and Germany.
A Roman bridge at Ilipoula (modern Niebla), spanning the Iberos/Luxia river (modern Rio Tinto).
A mountain in modern Turkey's İzmir province that was probably known as "Olympos" in antiquity.
A mountain, located within the modern French commune of Saint-Georges-Nigremont (a placename that echoes the ancient name of the mountain).
Nigris fl. (Djedi river) is a wadi in Algeria that is also one of the largest rivers of the Sahara.
Nigrum Pullum was a castellum along the Roman frontier in Germania Inferior. The archaeological site is located in modern Zwammerdam in the Netherlands.
According to Strabo, Alexander founded Nikaia in order to celebrate his victory over Porus.
Known today as Tenerife, this is the largest of the Canary islands.

The Assyrian king Sargon II (r. 721–705 BC) surrounded his new capital Dūr-Šarrukīn ("Fort Sargon") with a rectangular-shaped, 16,280-cubit-long inner and outer city wall. The name of the outer/lower city wall (šalḫû) was Ninurta-mukīn-temmēn-ālišu-ana-labār-ūmē-rūqūti ("The God Ninurta Is the One Who Establishes the Foundation of His City for (All) Days to Come") according to some Akkadian royal
An ancient Parthian fortress containing two settlement mounds, the tells of Old and New Nisa.
A sanctuary on Mont Sacon at an elevation of 1541 meters above sea level.
The Nitiobroges were an ancient tribe of southwestern Gaul.
An ancient people, tribe, or cultural group. Located: Wadi Natrun.
A hamlet in Sicily, located near Acireale, that is the findspot of antiquities possibly related to the ancient settlement of Acium.
Gate providing access from the northwest through the citadel defense walls at Dura-Europos.
Religious structure in Kythnos constructed in the Archaic period.

A Romano-British villa was identified at Norton Disney in 1933. This villa site has its origins in the first century CE and continued in use until the mid-fourth century. There were several architectural phases, the most elaborate of which included a corridor-type villa, a bath complex, a basilica-type hall, and a system of perimeter defenses.

Nostra Segnora de Mesumundu ("Our Lady of Mesumundu") is located in the territory of Siligo, Sardinia, Italy. This archaeological site preserves remains of multiple architectural phases. A mid-Imperial (likely second-century CE) Roman complex, which included baths, was reused, in part, for the construction of a Christian church in the sixth century.
A pre-Roman and Gallo-Roman sanctuary at the locality called l'Ermitage de Notre-Dame-de-Laval.
Rocky islands described as being 25 stades from Paphos, Cyprus.
Novaesium (modern Neuss) was a Roman castrum along the German frontier (limes) founded ca. 16 B.C.
The chief base of the Roman fleet on the lower Danube river.

Cemetery site located on the banks of the Chigla River, near the modern village of Novaya Chigla, Voronezh Oblast. The site contains 28 burials associated with the Srubnaya Culture (Late Bronze Age 1900-1200 BCE) and the Sarmatians (1st-2nd centuries CE).
A Roman road station located along the ancient route leading from Berenike to Edfu (the ancient Apollinopolis Magna).
The Temple of Apedemak, also known as the Lion Temple, is located to the west of the temple of Amun.
Numana was a settlement of ancient Picenum located south of Ancona.
A nuragic village dating ca. 1600 BC.
A nuragic complex in northwest Sardinia.
A single-tower nuragic site; the diameter of the tower measures ca. 12 meters.
A Middle Bronze Age nuragic site (ca. 1500 BC) near Cagliari, Sardinia.

A nuragic site located near Chia, Sardinia, Su Nuraxi de Baccu Idda is located atop a 78 m hill close to the course of the Riu di Chia, a stream that irrigates the plain south-east of the nuragic complex.
Nuraghe Bardalazzu, a ruined nuragic site located near Dualchi, Sardinia.
A nuraghe that is located atop a trachytic rock at a bend in the Rio d'Aridda, a river that has carved a deep valley.
A nuragic site of the Middle Bronze Age near Oristano, Sardinia.
A nuragic monument near Silanus, Sardinia, constructed primarily of granite and rising to a height of ca. 12 m and dating to the Middle to Late Bronze Age (seventeenth to ninth centuries BC).

Nuraghe Ponte, Dualchi is located near the archaeological complex of Frenegarzu. The site consists of a single circular tower (diameter 13.25 m; height 11.80 m) built upon a foundation of large roughly-hewn polyhedral blocks that support the structure built of neatly squared ashlars.
A complex nuraghe surrounded by a quadrilobate bastion.
A nuraghe located near Tottubella in the territory of Sassari.
A nuragic complex dating ca. 1500 BC near Tortolì in Sardinia.
A nuragic structure dating originally ca. 1,600 to 1,450 BC.
A nuraghe located near Sas Contreddas, Sardinia.
A nuragic site in northeast Sardinia, it was occupied from the fourteenth until the ninth century BC. At its height, the complex covered approximately five hectares.
A Nuragic settlement that pre-dates and, in some cases, is re-occupied during the Roman period.

The Nybgenii, a civitas mentioned in a series of second-century CE inscriptions, occupied a territory that extended to Chareb on the north bank of Chott el-Fejaj and had as its center the oasis of Telmine in present-day Nefzaoua, according to Encyclopédie berbère.

An elaborate nymphaeum on the Oppian Hill discovered in 1895. The complex dates to the Late Republican period. The ancient nymphaeum was partially obliterated by the construction of the Neronian Domus Aurea.
Known today as the Isola di Foradada, this small, prominent limestone islet lies just off the Sardinian Capo Caccia.

Buddhist monastery and educational center founded during the Gupta Empire (5th century CE). The site was destroyed around 1200 CE. It was located in ancient and medieval Magadha (modern-day Bihar), eastern India.
The Bahariya Oasis is a depression and oasis located in the Western Desert of Egypt approximately 370 km from Cairo.
Oaxus lacus, the modern lake Zorkul (or Sir-i-kol), is a lake located in the Pamir Mountains along the border between Afghanistan and Tajikistan.
Oberaden was the site of a Roman fort used during the Germanic Wars of Drusus.
The modern River Liffey flows from Liffey Head Bog to the Irish Sea.
The Oboulensioi were an ancient people of Moesia Inferior.
Ocra M. (Mt. Nanos) is a karst limestone plateau located at the eastern border of the Slovenian Littoral.
An ancient building at Aphrodisias that is referred to both as a bouleuterion and an odeion.

The Odeon at Kom el-Dikka, used both for entertainment and academic functions, was built in the center of ancient Alexandria in the fourth century CE and rebuilt between the end of the fifth and beginning of the sixth century CE.
A large theater in Athens, built during the Roman period on the south-western slope of the Acropolis around 160 to 174 CE.
The Odeon is a small theater in modern day Lyon, France built specifically for musical performances around the beginning of the 2nd century CE.

A promontory of southeastern Sicily that is connected to the journey of Odysseus. The location is correlated with the coastal marshland known as Pantano Longarini, a wetland area covering some 200 ha located in the province of Ragusa, Sicily.
The modern Livadostras river, emptying into the Corinthian Gulf near ancient Kreusis.
Oescus was originally a Thracian city at the confluence of the Danube and Iskar rivers,
The Oescus river (modern Iskar) is a river of Bulgaria and tributary of the Danube.
A mountain range of southern Phthiotis and northern Phocis in Greece, Oeta is celebrated in mythology as the site of Herakles' death.
The Oguz Kurgan is the site of an elite Scythian burial dating to the fourth century BCE.
Oechalia in Euboea, possible archaeological traces of which may be found at the site of Kastri/Ano Potamia.
An ancient fortified settlement and deme of Attica. The archaeological site is located to the east of modern Oinoe/Inoi (formerly Mazi).
A fortress of the ancient Corinthia captured by Agesilaus II of Sparta in 390 B.C.
An ancient river of the Peloponnese peninsula that flows into the Eurotas River near the site of Sparta.
The largest of the ancient Oinoussai islands, a small group of islands lying between the island of Chios and the Ionian peninsula.

A Roman fort and a series of five associated enclosures situated on a hilltop overlooking the valley of the River Okement to the northwest and Okehampton town to the southwest. Excavations suggest that the site was occupied ca. A.D. 50-80.
The Olba Aqueduct is located in Mersin Province of southern Turkey. It was commissioned during the reign of Septimius Severus and restored under Justinian I.
The tell of Old Nisa is part of the Parthian fortress of Nisa, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Old Temple of Athena Polias at Athens
Archaic temple to Athena built on the Athenian Acropolis likely during the second half of the 6th century BC. Likely destroyed during the Persian invasion in 480 BC.
An Iron Age hillfort located in Kent that dates to the first century A.D. and shows signs for at least partial reorganization following the Roman invasion of Britain.
The Ollius River (modern Oglio) is a tributary of the Po River in northern Italy.
The Olona river flows through the provinces of Varese, Milan and Pavia and empties into the Lambro meridionale.
An ancient settlement on the Athos/Akte peninsula.
Olygyrtos M. is a mountain located at the point where the reigons of Arcadia, the Corinthia and the Argolid intersect in the northeastern Peloponnese.
Olympus is the highest mountain in Greece, located in the Olympus Range. In Greek mythology, it is the home of the Olympian gods.

Omega House is the modern name for a large house on the north slope of the Areopagos hill in Athens. Early traces go back to the 4th century BC, but the surviving structure was built in the 4th and 5th centuries AD. It appears to have been a philosophical school until the 6th century. It was destroyed in the Slavic Sack of 582 AD.
Onchesmos was a port in Epirus.
A place in Africa Proconsularis included on the Peutinger map.
